title: What Power Resilience Districts Is
definition: Power Resilience Districts: districts keeping power through outages.
description:
Power Resilience Districts is districts keeping power through outages. It sits squarely in Future Safety & Civilization Resilience, the frontier where microgrids science becomes district logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are critical loads-scale. Societies that master district hulls early will shape islanding practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why microgrids programs worldwide now treat Power Resilience Districts as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Power Resilience Districts needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

definition: Today's documented research behind Power Resilience Districts.
description:
The road to Power Resilience Districts is already being paved. The Global Health Security Index benchmarks national pandemic readiness. FEMA's resilient-infrastructure programs and the EU Civil Protection Mechanism coordinate disaster response.

The WHO's pandemic preparedness treaty negotiations build global early-warning systems. Together these programs form the microgrids foundation that Power Resilience Districts will build on — the district logistics results, the islanding methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as district logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Power Resilience Districts
definition: Estimates Power Resilience Districts readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Power Resilience Districts components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a district hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Power Resilience Districts Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Power Resilience Districts operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Power Resilience Districts installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 95431 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where microgrids monitoring, district logistics redundancy, or islanding maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Power Resilience Districts Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Power Resilience Districts: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Power Resilience Districts — districts keeping power through outages.

Phase 1 — Prove (microgrids): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (district logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (islanding): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (critical loads): district hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cities-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
